description: This pie chart illustrates the distribution of different task categories within a benchmark, divided into 11 distinct slices. There is no separate legend; instead, each segment is directly labeled along its outer edge with the category name, a raw count, and a percentage in parentheses, all formatted in bold text. None of the slices are exploded or visually offset. Visually, the segments are arranged in descending order of size, progressing counter-clockwise starting from the top-left. The largest slice is "ObservationAngle" in mint green at 126 (12.28%), followed by "SimilarMaterial" in orange at 106 (10.33%), "SubEvent" in pinkish-red at 100 (9.74%), and "UsageSimilarity" in coral at 100 (9.65%). Continuing counter-clockwise, four consecutive slices share an identical count of 90 and a proportion of 8.77%: "Environment" in teal, "Layout" in pale yellow, "AppearanceSimilarity" in light green, and "SimilarEvent" in cornflower blue. These are followed by "MentalitySimilarity" in cyan at 89 (8.67%) and "RelativePosition" in light grey at 81 (7.90%). The smallest category, completing the circle at the top, is "NearSameEntity" in dark grey at 63 (6.34%).
caption_used: The pie chart illustrates the distribution of different tasks in the MMRA benchmark, with a total of 11 categories represented. The largest category, 'ObservationAngle,' accounts for approximately 15% of the total samples, while 'SimilarMaterial' and 'SubEvent' follow closely at 12% and 11%, respectively. 'NearSameEntity,' the smallest category, represents only 5% of the benchmark. The chart highlights that 'Environment' and 'Layout' have identical proportions, each contributing 10% to the dataset. The percentages within each slice are labeled for clarity, and the chart is color-coded to distinguish the categories effectively.
